thread:
Asha: Hey team — FIRMWAVE (customer) reported a spike of 429s this morning on their dedicated pool in eu-west-1. They say it started around 07:12 UTC and lasted ~8m. They're seeing rejections even though they have reserved capacity.

Ida: Ack, can you drop the error payload they see? Any headers like X-RateLimit or pool id?

Asha: Pasting a sample curl response they captured: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 09 May 2023 07:15:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1652087703
{"error":"rate limit exceeded","pool":"reserved-eu-west-1-pool-9"}
```

Asha: Their config shows reserved QPS = 1000 and burst capacity = 200. They claim sustained traffic was ~950 QPS with a short burst to 1350 QPS for ~45s.

Liam: Hmm — if Remaining=0 and Reset aligns to a token-bucket refill, looks like the global per-route enforcement also kicked in. Need to check the runtime logs to confirm if it was pool throttle or global route limit.

Noah: I noticed a deploy around 07:10 from deploy-bot to routing rules (deploy id dpl-778). @Liam can you confirm whether the policy change adjusted route-level QPS or added stricter cross-tenant caps?

deploy-bot: Deployed routing-policy v2.3 to eu-west-1 at 07:09:54 UTC by noah_g. Changes: fallback routing tweaks, no direct per-tenant caps changed. :rocket:

Liam: OK deploy didn't change per-tenant caps but it did add a new "cost-aware" fallback. That shouldn't reduce reserved pool headroom, but if the pool was temporarily dry and smart-routing moved some requests to fallback group, it might have triggered additional rate checks.

Ida: Customer is asking for repro steps we can run. Asha — can you share a minimal repro (curl/ab) we can run against their pool-id or a synthetic that mimics their burst?

Asha: Suggested repro command we gave them (and we ran in staging):

```
# 60s test: steady 900 QPS then burst 1400 for 60s
ab -n 120000 -c 900 -s 60 http://api.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/generate
# then spike with a short script sending concurrent requests to reach ~1400 qps
```

Noah: I'm going to pull the pool metrics (token-bucket usage, queued requests, reject counts) and the route limiter logs for that interval. Also will check KV-cache pressure — large model context can increase per-request cost and effectively reduce tokens/sec.

Liam: Hypotheses: (1) reserved pool token bucket max allowed burst smaller than customer expects (burst config applied per-minute), (2) global per-route limit suppressed fallback, (3) latency increases causing longer in-flight times -> lower effective throughput -> token exhaustion.

Ida: Can you add these checks to the thread: 
- pool id matched: reserved-eu-west-1-pool-9 (Asha)
- sample request-id list (from customer): req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789
- customer SLA claim: 99.5% availability, desired no-429 for bursts up to +50% for <60s.

Noah: Pulled metrics: token-bucket show reserve=1000 qps, burst_window=60s, burst_tokens=200. At 07:13:xx bucket hit zero and reject rate spiked. We also see 120s of slightly elevated p95 latency for the model backend starting 07:11, which amplified in-flight durations.

Liam: Can you paste the runtime limiter log lines around 07:13? We need to see whether the reject was from "pool-throttle" or "route-global".

Noah: excerpt: 
```
[07:12:59] limiter=pool-throttle pool_id=reserved-eu-west-1-pool-9 action=reject reason="tokens=0" req=req_abc123
[07:13:01] limiter=pool-throttle pool_id=reserved-eu-west-1-pool-9 action=reject reason="tokens=0" req=req_def456
[07:13:02] limiter=route-global route=/v1/generate action=reject reason="global-cap" req=req_ghi789
```

Asha: So both: pool exhausted then some global rejections as well. That matches customer experience.

Ida: Next steps? Customer wants a mitigation ASAP (they're on dedicated with SLA) — recommended temporary options: (a) increase guaranteed reserved QPS, (b) raise burst window/tokens, (c) enable cross-regional spillover to their backup reserved pool. Any risk in (b)?

Liam: (b) is safe short-term but can impact overall capacity fairness. (a) requires billing/contract change if beyond committed capacity. (c) is acceptable if their account is configured with backup pools — need to check tenancy mapping.

Noah: For immediate mitigation I suggest: bump burst_tokens to 400 for 30m and toggle spillover to their eu-central reserved pool. I'll open an RB change and run a quick synthetic.

Ida: Please coordinate with support to get customer's approval for temporary changes and capture timeline. Also create a CS ticket for billing if we extend guaranteed QPS.

Asha: I've messaged the customer to request permission for temporary burst bump and asked for a time window. They replied OK for immediate mitigation for 30m.

Noah: Done — applied burst_tokens=400 and enabled spillover to reserved-eu-central-7 at 07:24. Monitoring now.

Liam: After the change we should re-run the synthetic: 
```
# replay same pattern
ab -n 120000 -c 900 -s 60 http://api.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/generate
# spike to 1400 qps and watch rejects
```

Noah: Post-mitigation logs: rejects dropped from ~420 to 12 during the spike window, latency p95 improved slightly. No global-cap rejects after spillover.

Ida: Customer confirmed they saw fewer 429s during the spike and are OK with the temporary mitigation. Ask billing for a PO or formal increase if they want permanent capacity.

Asha: I'll file follow-up: 1) customer-facing summary + timeline, 2) ask for billing PO if they want committed increase, 3) recommend runbook entries to document mapping between reserved pool burst_tokens and visible X-RateLimit headers.

Liam: Action items: 
- Noah: write a short postmortem paragraph and add instrumentation to make pool-throttle visible in tenant dashboard (due EOD).
- Ida: update customer with summary and next steps (billing).
- Asha: attach repro commands and test results to support ticket.

Ida: Marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark: Will re-open if we see repeat behavior.

Asha: Thanks all. 

ratebot: Incident classification: "capacity-exhaustion" (priority P2) — created incident INC-2023-4763.

Noah: I'll follow up with a durable fix — likely adjust burst accounting to be more permissive for short sub-60s spikes on dedicated pools when SLA indicates allowed bursts.

Liam: Nice triage. Leaving notes in eng-runbook about verifying token-bucket semantics when routing policies change. :eyes:"
